title: Hubble reveals a super-rich galactic neighborhood
caption: The galaxy cluster Abell 1413, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Abell 1413 · constellation Leo · about 2 billion light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows the galaxy cluster Abell 1413, over 2 billion light-years from Earth between the constellations of Leo and Coma Berenices. The scene is dominated by a large, strongly elliptical galaxy called MCG+04-28-097, whose halo of stars stretches for more than 6.5 million light-years.

Abell 1413 is called rich because it holds a huge number of galaxies, more than 300, bound together by the cluster's powerful gravity. Interactions among them heat the material in the cluster to almost 100 million degrees, so the cluster gives off strong X-rays.

The cluster also shows faint arcs. These come from gravitational lensing, in which the cluster's intense gravity bends space-time around it, distorting the light of galaxies that lie farther behind it into strange, stretched shapes.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.16 x 1.69 arcminutes) and distance (2 billion light years), the frame spans roughly 1.8 million × 983,000 light-years. Its light set out about 2,000 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image was made from optical and near-infrared exposures with the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using filters at 775 and 814 nm. The color mapping is not published.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and a cluster this distant is far too faint to see without long exposures from a telescope like Hubble.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble & NASAAcknowledgement: Nick Rose

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Abell 1413 is part of the Abell catalog of over 4000 rich galaxy clusters, all relatively close in astronomical terms, whose light has traveled for less than 3 billion years to get here. Galaxies near the cluster's center are very elongated, while those farther out are rounder. A version of this image was entered by Nick Rose into the Hubble's Hidden Treasures processing competition.
alt: A crowded field of galaxies dominated by a large, elongated elliptical galaxy, with faint arcs of distorted light.
